title: Connected technology is becoming essential infrastructure, but consumer value now depends on reliability, support, trust, and total ownership cost
source_unit: Assurant, 2026 Global Connected Consumer Trends Report
geography: Global online consumer sentiment survey across connected-device users, with market snapshots including the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, Japan, India, Mexico, and Australia

consumer_orientation.value: consumers are broadly positive about technology but express concerns about cost, complexity, and trust

expectation_shift.value: expectations increasingly concern performance, simplicity, support, and who is trusted to deliver the experience

observations.method: Assurant online quantitative survey of compensated adults aged 18 and older who use smartphones, with country samples quota-balanced across key demographics; composite index built from 34 questions across five dimensions.
observations.uncertainty: The source is company-sponsored consumer research, uses an online panel, and measures reported attitudes rather than observed device use, spending, support outcomes, or long-run retention.
observations.subgroup: Connected-device users in global and national market frames, with differing device mixes, income, housing, age, employment, trust, and access to repair or support.
observations.counterinterpretation: A positive sentiment index can coexist with frustration, unequal access, platform dependence, and dissatisfaction with particular devices or service routes.

observations.period: 2026 report; six shifts in connected-consumer expectations

local_relevance.value: global technology strategies require local relevance rather than one-size-fits-all protection

ownership_cost.value: protection value is increasingly judged through total cost of ownership and product longevity

support_differentiation.value: support is framed as a differentiator when devices become essential and more complex

ai_complexity.value: AI is increasing both capability and complexity in connected technology

observations.method: Comparative interpretation of global survey results, device frustration, support preferences, protection interest, and market snapshots.
observations.uncertainty: The six shifts are an interpretive framework from a commercial provider and do not establish market-wide causal effects or independent evidence that protection improves welfare.
observations.subgroup: Consumers managing device purchase, ownership, repair, replacement, protection, privacy, and support decisions; device makers, carriers, retailers, and service providers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Consumers may value reliability and support without purchasing an Assurant-linked protection product; preferences can reflect local prices, device quality, warranty rules, or market structure.

us_life_improvement.unit: percent saying connected technology has improved their lives

us_protection_interest_ai_smartphone.unit: percent more likely to consider protection for AI-enabled smartphones

us_support_route.value: consumers report using self-help, friends and family, manuals, and AI tools to solve device problems

observations.method: Country market snapshot from the Assurant Technology Sentiment Index survey and reported device-support, AI, and protection measures.
observations.uncertainty: The snapshot is descriptive and company-sponsored; shares are not a causal test of AI trust, protection enrollment, device retention, or consumer welfare.
observations.subgroup: US smartphone users with different ages, genders, housing, employment, education, device ecosystems, and access to self-help or paid support.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported AI trust and life improvement can coexist with privacy concerns, poor connectivity, storage constraints, support friction, or inability to replace a device.

observations.period: 2026 report; connected-device ownership and brand relationship

denominator.unit: global connected-device ownership and support frame

support_continuity.value: protection, service, and support shape whether consumers choose, keep, and engage with connected technology over time

personalization.value: personalized protection and support are framed as more relevant than standardized coverage

brand_value.value: the report positions relevant, flexible support as a route to stronger brand perception and loyalty

observations.method: Synthesis of survey responses about protection-plan interest, support preferences, device problems, and brand perception across country snapshots.
observations.uncertainty: The report is partly an industry strategy document; reported brand effects are not independent measures of actual loyalty, retention, claims resolution, or consumer surplus.
observations.subgroup: Connected consumers, households managing repair and replacement risk, brands, carriers, retailers, protection providers, support channels, and platform ecosystems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Personalization can increase complexity, data collection, lock-in, and unequal treatment; support that improves brand perception may still shift repair or replacement costs to consumers.

related_sources.claim: Assurant publication context for the 2026 connected-consumer report.

boundary: This record adds a consumer-technology, ownership, support, trust, AI, and market-infrastructure route. It uses a company-sponsored aggregate survey and report synthesis, not respondent-level ingestion, observed transaction or claims data, a causal estimate of protection or support effects, an independent audit of AI trust, or proof that connected technology produces equal welfare across markets.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Assurant 2026 Global Connected Consumer Trends Report PDF reviewed for the global Technology Sentiment Index, six market shifts, US market snapshot, support routes, AI trust, protection interest, and ownership-value conclusions.
